target_verification.reason: Official ALA and Oodi pages identify the building, three-level concept, top-floor Book Heaven, Citizens' Balcony, arching wood volume, undulating ceiling, and double-helix stair. Exact camera-area dimensions and furniture placement remain inferred.

scene_goal: A complete concept interior of Helsinki Central Library Oodi's top-floor Book Heaven reading room, emphasizing the quiet open reading landscape and its public balcony edge.
relationships: The open reading floor is the dominant central space.
The curved timber volume anchors the rear edge and visually connects down through the building.
The Citizens' Balcony runs along the glazed city-facing edge.
The double-helix stair is a vertical landmark beside the timber volume.
Reading oases and book stacks sit as islands in the open floor, while the cafe stays near the balcony edge.

visual_language.style: contemporary Finnish civic interior, open and calm, with an expressive curved timber spine
visual_language.lighting: cool diffuse daylight through the glazed facade balanced by warm pendant pools over reading islands
visual_language.mood: quiet, bright, civic, generous and slightly futuristic

must_have: undulating white ceiling with circular skylights
hard_constraints: Keep the building identity as Oodi and the modeled scope as the top-floor reading environment.
Preserve a strong public edge: open floor toward the balcony and city view.
Use wood, glass and white acoustic surfaces as the dominant architectural language.
Do not present inferred dimensions as measured facts.
soft_constraints: Use a 1:1 metric concept scale with a readable 28 m x 18 m selected area.
Keep furniture low-poly but make the main architectural silhouettes coherent.
Use a single hero camera that shows the timber volume, stair, reading floor and balcony together.
uncertainties: Selected camera area and furniture arrangement are inferred.
Exact wave ceiling geometry and stair geometry are simplified for a complete concept scene.
